target_customer: Pharma partners and patients with short-telomere diseases such as pulmonary fibrosis and liver disease
problem: Short telomeres underlie several fatal diseases and aging. The company develops transient mRNA therapies that extend telomeres in cells without permanent genetic changes.
business_model: Preclinical biotech developing mRNA therapeutics, funded by venture equity and government grants; revenue would come from licensing or drug sales
product_category: mRNA therapeutics (telomere extension, TERT mRNA in lipid nanoparticles)

founders.name: John Ramunas
education: Stanford University, PhD (thesis on telomere extension, Helen Blau lab)
founders.background_notes: Company site and BioSpace (Sept 2023) say he is a co-inventor with a decade of therapeutic mRNA experience. YC page says he invented TERT mRNA telomere extension in the Blau lab.

founders.name: Glenn Markov
education: Stanford University, PhD in Genetics (YC page lists 2018)
founders.background_notes: Company site says a decade of experience in genetics and epigenetics of cellular reprogramming.

founders.name: Helen Blau
founders.background_notes: BioSpace calls her a co-founder; the company site lists her as Founder and Advisor.

competitors.name: Sierra Sciences
competitors.what: Screened small molecules to activate telomerase for anti-aging
competitors.traction_then: Reported more than 200 telomerase-inducing compounds in 29 drug families; none judged strong enough by one reviewer

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires a new mRNA and lipid nanoparticle therapeutic to be proven safe and effective in humans, with IND-enabling toxicology and clinical trials. Efficacy so far is preclinical (mouse fibrosis models per NIH abstracts).

defensibility.rationale: The company states 40+ granted patents (site) based on Stanford-origin telomere extension work, and drug approval creates regulatory barriers. Small-molecule and supplement approaches were different mechanisms.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found shows an incumbent copying or buying the telomere mRNA approach through 2025.

market_need_then: Short telomeres are linked to fatal diseases such as pulmonary fibrosis, which have limited treatments, and the company's lead programs target these. Public interest in longevity and mRNA therapeutics had grown by the time of the 2023 seed.

branding.domain_note: Company uses rejuvenationtech.com, not the exact .com of the full name.

identity.voice_and_tone: Science-forward claims such as rewinding cellular aging clocks

brand_strength.rationale: A descriptive, somewhat generic name typical of biotech. The company holds many trademarks for product names (aggregators disagree on 18 versus 90) but no evidence of public brand pull.

outcome_analysis: The company is a preclinical biotech built on Stanford telomere work by its founders. It took until September 2023 to announce a $10.6M seed led by Khosla, plus grants, and was still heading toward IND-enabling work with no trial dosing reported. Success depends on clinical data that does not yet exist publicly, so the story is so far one of credible science and grant-supported progress rather than a proven outcome.
notes: Founding year conflicts: YC says 2018, a conference bio cited in search says 2016. The grant amount of $4.6M is as of the September 2023 announcement and may span earlier years. Company site says over $8M in grants awarded since 2023; the two figures are not reconciled. The seed was announced 5 years after the YC batch, so any earlier financing is unknown. An aggregator lists LifeSpan Vision Ventures as a seed lead; the press release does not, so it was ignored. FDA INTERACT is a pre-IND consultation, not an IND clearance. Competitor list is thin: only one source dated before the batch was found. The Sierra Sciences description comes from a search result for the 2011 post, which was not opened.
